The stakes have never been higher.
#
Peter — when you chip in toward our campaign to defeat Josh Hawley and elect Lucas Kunce, **you’re investing in the most competitive and affordable chance we have to flip a GOP U.S. Senate seat this year.**
**[CHIP IN NOW →](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/44620?refcode=em20240317-5065&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=5065%2E614464%2EBhUH7e)**
Here’s what makes Missouri’s U.S. Senate race our most cost-effective opportunity to flip a GOP-held U.S. Senate seat this November:
1. **Josh Hawley is seriously vulnerable.** In 2018, he won his Senate seat with only 51% of the vote — and after he exposed himself to be a fraud and a coward on January 6, his approval ratings became the worst of any GOP Senator running for re-election in 2024.
2. **Lucas Kunce is already in a _statistical tie_ with Hawley.** Multiple polls put Lucas and Hawley in a margin-of-error race for Missouri’s U.S. Senate seat.
3. **Missourians have a history of taking back their power at the ballot box.** Since his last election, voters have broken with Hawley to approve measures that raised the minimum wage, expanded healthcare, and legalized weed with huge margins of victory. And after major recent wins for red state Democrats in Kentucky and Ohio, Missouri is next.
4. **Every $1 in Missouri can go nearly five times as far compared to states like Texas and Florida.** Our state has small media markets, which means we’ll be able to reach Missourians with Lucas’ message early and often — on TV, online, and on the ground.
5. **The stakes have never been higher.** With abortion rights and control of the U.S. Senate on the line this year, we can’t afford to let this opportunity here in Missouri go to waste.

Lucas Kunce is working hard to build the record-breaking, worker-led coalition that can take advantage of this moment and flip Missouri’s U.S. Senate seat.
**But with GOP insiders already spending millions of dollars to attack Lucas and prop up Hawley’s campaign, we need your help to do it, Peter.**
Missouri’s election-winning labor movement has started to unite behind Lucas — along with elected officials, community leaders, national organizations, and everyday people all across the state. But winning this race will be determined by our ability to keep up this grassroots momentum. So please:
**[Will you add a donation of $10 or whatever you can afford toward our campaign to replace Josh Hawley and elect Lucas Kunce to Missouri’s U.S. Senate seat? Our campaign doesn’t accept a penny from corporate PACs, so your early support really does make a big difference.](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/44620?refcode=em20240317-5065&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=5065%2E614464%2EBhUH7e)**

Peter,

I’ve been thinking about this Bible verse a lot lately:

_“Then Peter and the other apostles answered and said, We ought to obey God rather than men” - Acts 5:29_

I think it’s a lesson a lot of politicians could take to heart.

Too many members of Congress have completely lost sight of what we were put here to do, Peter. Instead of defending our God-given freedoms, they want to take them away for power and riches.

**It’s time to bring Faith back to America.**

Now, they're directly targeting Kirsten's seat to retake Senate control. I know that my friend has what it takes to defeat the GOP and their megadonors. But because she refuses to accept money from corporate PACs, she's counting on strong grassroots support to win this critical race.= | | = Thank you for taking the time to support my friend and help defend our Senate majority. With gratitude, Chuck Schumer | * | = A note from Kirsten: Friend, I can’t thank you enough for standing by my side in the critical fights ahead of us. As Democrats face our toughest Senate map in decades, I need your help more than ever. While Republicans only have to defend 10 seats in 2024, Democrats have to defend 23 — and if the GOP flips just two of them, it will deliver Senate control back to Mitch McConnell. Now, experts at FiveThirtyEight are saying that the GOP has a clear path to the majority. As right-wing special interests gear up to pour millions into flipping the Senate, we need to fight back right now. But I refuse to take a single cent from corporate PACs, which means I’m relying on your grassroots support. = And if you’d like to become a core member of my team and receive exclusive texts from my campaign, = Thank you, Kirsten Gillibrand

Hi PeterI hope this e-mail finds you well and ready for the weekend. It’s John Edgar, candidate for Colorado’s 5thCongressional District, and I wanted to personally update you on our recent efforts and what’s coming up.
# What Happened This Week?

This past week was our best one yet! John hosted many events and met with several delegates. John and his team are securing more votes each and every day and we are grateful to each of our delegates who have made the commitment to vote for us on April 6th!

# Campaign Highlights
-We are mailing out hundreds of letters to delegates to personally ask them for their vote!-We are scheduling one-on-ones throughout the next few weeks to get a sense of what issues matter most to our delegates and to answer any questions. -We are STILL making hundreds of calls every week! We are following up with texts and emails.-We are raising more and more money each week, primarily from small donors. Shout out to everyone who has contributed to our cause!-We are growing the team and continuing to recruit new volunteers!-We will be knocking on doors to personally meet with any delegate we have been unable to contact.
Throughout this entire campaign, John has led with integrity and has played by the rules. John will continue this fight with virtue so that he can represent EVERYONE in CD5 when he gets to Washington in November.
John listens and he will fight for the issues YOU care about. Our team will outwork everyone else to get on the ballot, win the primary, and then win office in the general. Thank you for joining us in this adventure!

As we work to make your voice heard and strive to change the tone in Washington, we need your help. Please consider [donating](https://vote4edgar.us12.list-manage.com/track/click?u=9d3a666e5996be881f1745f2f&id=d07e8e4f1c&e=add163c1a3) if you can. Everything helps and I sincerely appreciate you. Together we can move the needle in our Nation’s capital and together we can _**Choose Common Sense Over Chaos**_.
**John**

| **March 17, 2024**
# **SUNDAY NEWS DIGEST**
### By Heidi Ganahl
---
| Good evening, Happy Saint Patrick's Day! I hope your weekend was filled with corned beef and cabbage (more on this as our fun fact of the day below), green beer, and the luck o' the Irish! As we delve into the ongoing legislative session in Colorado, the tally of introduced bills stands at 556 -- a very high volume for this early stage of session. We've been following [Kevin Lundberg's great reporting](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) on "Good Bills" and "Bad Bills" passing through committees and worth fighting for/against. Here's a short list of some of the bills he shared this week. Read his [full list](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) here. **Good Bills:**
* [HB24-1041](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) Streamline Filing Sales & Use Tax Returns: While it may seem minor, this bill aims to simplify the process of filing sales and use tax returns, offering a small but welcome relief to taxpayers. It has successfully passed the Senate second reading.
* [HB24-1065](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) Reduction of State Income Tax Rate: This initiative seeks to lower the state income tax rate from 4.4% to 4.0%, providing potential financial relief to hardworking Coloradans. Unfortunately, it was stalled in the first committee.
* [HB24-1106](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) Require Information about Abortion Pill Reversal: This proposal aimed to ensure that information about abortion pill reversal options is readily available with chemical abortion products. It was halted in the first committee.
* [HB24-1128](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) Enforcement of Federal Immigration Law: Advocating for a more sensible approach to immigration law, this bill sought to align Colorado law with federal statutes. However, it faced opposition and was defeated in the first committee.
* [HB24-1029](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) Prohibit Foreign Ownership Agriculture & Natural Resources: As Lundberg noted, the title says it all. This was unshockingly killed in first committee.

**Bad Bills:**
* [HB24-1017](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) Bill of Rights for Foster Youth: This bill, purportedly aiming to protect foster youth, risks marginalizing foster families who do not adhere to transgender ideology. Unfortunately, it passed the House, raising concerns about its potential impact.
* [HB24-1039](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) Non-Legal Name Changes: Mandating public schools to accommodate students' preferred pronouns and concealing transitioning information from parents, this bill poses significant parental rights and educational concerns. Regrettably, it advanced to the third reading in the House.
* [HB24-1040](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) Gender-Affirming Health-Care Provider Study: Presented as a study, this bill could incentivize medical facilities to facilitate life-altering procedures for children, raising ethical and medical concerns.
* [HB24-1071](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) Name Change to Conform with Gender Identity: Allowing incarcerated individuals to change their legal names based on gender identity, this bill raises questions about its practical implications and potential misuse.
* [HB24-1174](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) Concealed Carry Permits & Training: Transferring concealed carry instruction to the Colorado Bureau of Investigation, this bill may hinder law-abiding citizens' access to permits and training, potentially infringing on Second Amendment rights.

Stay informed, stay vigilant, and let's work together to ensure that our state remains true to our conservative principles. Have a great week, Heidi Ganahl

Colorado budget writers may be headed back to the drawing board. Slower population growth and rising fee revenue could trigger upwards of $300 million more state taxpayer refunds than expected in the current budget year, under economic forecasts presented to the Joint Budget Committee on Friday. The latest forecasts leave top lawmakers well short of what they expected to be able to spend in next year’s budget, with less than a week left to finalize the 2024-25 spending plan before it has to be submitted to the General Assembly for consideration. [**Legislators at odds on broadband right-of-way fees**](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) [COLORADO POLITICS](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) Michael Fiore, the outreach coordinator for Voices for Awareness and Project Facing Fentanyl, remembered selling drugs to support his addiction and skating through the system before getting clean — after serving a prison term in New York. # NATIONAL
**[Feds investigating Meta for possible role in illegal drug sales on Facebook, Instagram](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [NEW YORK POST](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**The feds are poking Facebook for possible drug dealing. US prosecutors in Virginia are investigating Meta Platforms, the parent company of Facebook and Instagram, for playing a role in facilitating illegal drug sales online, the Wall Street Journal reported Saturday.
**[Biden pushing to erase voter ID requirements that are backed by 85% of voters](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [THE WASHINGTON TIMES](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**Recent comments from Biden administration officials have stirred a debate about the role of federal agencies in supporting citizen participation in elections and the validity of voter ID laws.
**[February inflation report a setback for Fed rate cut plans; prices up 3.2%](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [THE WASHINGTON POST](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) The Federal Reserve is looking for steady, reliable signs that inflation is simmering down before it cuts interest rates this year. So far, 2024 has not delivered. **[Teller County declares local disaster emergency as result of power outages, snowfall](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [CBS 11 KKTV](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**Teller County officials declared a local disaster emergency on Friday as a result of the winter storm. According to officials, the declaration was issued because “a public emergency exists in Teller County based on the severe winter storm and extremely high snow accumulation, which started on March 13, 2024, and continues, which poses an imminent threat of widespread and severe damage, injury or loss of life and property.”

**A collection of residents in Weld County argued, during a town hall meeting here Wednesday, they should have an opportunity to express opinions and engage with officials they elected.

# ☘️ DID YOU KNOW?

The meal that became a St. Patrick’s Day staple across the country—**corned beef and cabbage** —was an **American innovation**. While ham and cabbage were eaten in Ireland, corned beef offered a cheaper substitute for impoverished immigrants. Irish Americans living in the slums of lower Manhattan in the late 19th century and early 20th purchased leftover corned beef from ships returning from the tea trade in China. The Irish would boil the beef three times—the last time with cabbage—to remove some of the brine.

I hope your weekend was filled with corned beef and cabbage (more on this as our fun fact of the day below), green beer, and the luck o' the Irish! As we delve into the ongoing legislative session in Colorado, the tally of introduced bills stands at 556 -- a very high volume for this early stage of session. We've been following on "Good Bills" and "Bad Bills" passing through committees and worth fighting for/against. Here's a short list of some of the bills he shared this week. Read his here. Good Bills: Streamline Filing Sales & Use Tax Returns: While it may seem minor, this bill aims to simplify the process of filing sales and use tax returns, offering a small but welcome relief to taxpayers. It has successfully passed the Senate second reading. Reduction of State Income Tax Rate: This initiative seeks to lower the state income tax rate from 4.4% to 4.0%, providing potential financial relief to hardworking Coloradans. Unfortunately, it was stalled in the first committee. Require Information about Abortion Pill Reversal: This proposal aimed to ensure that information about abortion pill reversal options is readily available with chemical abortion products. It was halted in the first committee. Enforcement of Federal Immigration Law: Advocating for a more sensible approach to immigration law, this bill sought to align Colorado law with federal statutes. However, it faced opposition and was defeated in the first committee. Prohibit Foreign Ownership Agriculture & Natural Resources: As Lundberg noted, the title says it all. This was unshockingly killed in first committee. Bad Bills: Bill of Rights for Foster Youth: This bill, purportedly aiming to protect foster youth, risks marginalizing foster families who do not adhere to transgender ideology. Unfortunately, it passed the House, raising concerns about its potential impact. Non-Legal Name Changes: Mandating public schools to accommodate students' preferred pronouns and concealing transitioning information from parents, this bill poses significant parental rights and educational concerns. Regrettably, it advanced to the third reading in the House. Gender-Affirming Health-Care Provider Study: Presented as a study, this bill could incentivize medical facilities to facilitate life-altering procedures for children, raising ethical and medical concerns. Name Change to Conform with Gender Identity: Allowing incarcerated individuals to change their legal names based on gender identity, this bill raises questions about its practical implications and potential misuse. Concealed Carry Permits & Training: Transferring concealed carry instruction to the Colorado Bureau of Investigation, this bill may hinder law-abiding citizens' access to permits and training, potentially infringing on Second Amendment rights. Stay informed, stay vigilant, and let's work together to ensure that our state remains true to our conservative principles. The meal that became a St. Patrick’s Day staple across the country—corned beef and cabbage —was an American innovation. While ham and cabbage were eaten in Ireland, corned beef offered a cheaper substitute for impoverished immigrants. Irish Americans living in the slums of lower Manhattan in the late 19th century and early 20th purchased leftover corned beef from ships returning from the tea trade in China. The Irish would boil the beef three times—the last time with cabbage—to remove some of the brine. Dive deep into our journey against the odds, and see how you can make a real difference in 2026.

| | | |
---
(This email is longer than usual, but please read
all the way through to the end.)
**FELLOW PATRIOTS:**
Now that I've had some time to rest and reflect, I wanted to first say thank you for your support. Running for Congress has never been about me, but about all of us.
We, the grassroots, are gaining ground for the cause of liberty.
**Before we go any further, let me be clear about something...**
I am not a well-funded, well-connected politician trying to climb the political ladder for more power and influence. I am a working-class, self-employed small business owner living in this district as a constituent who is running for Congress because I am fed up with status-quo politicians who misrepresent the people.
_**Review of 2022 Texas Primaries**_
The 2022 Primaries in Texas found many in a new Congressional district, including myself. Texas added two new districts (we now have 38 districts instead of 36).
As some of you know, I announced my candidacy for TX-8 in late May 2021 and campaigned for that seat for the next 5-6 months.
After learning that my residence was no longer in TX-8 but was redistricted to TX-2, I decided to throw away the previous months of campaigning and run for the new district I found myself in.
It is not illegal to run to represent a district you don't reside in. But on principle, you should live in the district you are running to represent. And it was on that principle that I chose to run in TX-2.
Because of redistricting, there were talks of pushing the primary election to June, giving constituents and candidates a chance to become aware of the changes.
But it was all talk, and the primary election date wasn't changed. This left voters confused at the ballot box - which ultimately benefited incumbents.
This situation left our campaign only three months to campaign against our new opponent, Dan Crenshaw.
I was approached by someone who wanted to fund my campaign with a lot of money—and I mean **a lot**! But it would have required me to do something that violated my conscience.
Most might've seen it as a small ask, but to me; it was a test of whether I could be bought, so I turned it down.
Despite the limited timetable and raising only $45k, we took 17-18% of the vote.
Two others were also running against Crenshaw for the seat. We raised less than **$75k** between the three but gained 26% of the vote.
Meanwhile, Dan Crenshaw raised $10 Million, spent between $7-8 Million, and received 74% of the vote.
I knew that we weren't done and that I had no choice but to run again in 2024.
For the 2022 primaries, I had a campaign manager, a grassroots coordinator, two consultants, and over 100 volunteers.
Despite the team that I had, between running my business and campaigning, my workload was 18-20 hour days.
I knew we needed more help for 2024 and to build on what he had.
_**The 2024 Texas Primaries**_
I announced my candidacy for TX-2 in late January 2023 because I wanted to get a head start. After all, Dan Crenshaw is an incumbent who is a damn good fundraiser.
But then I found myself in a bit of a pickle...
My campaign manager and consultants didn't return for personal reasons.
Only a handful of volunteers remained after clearing out the "do-nothings" on my volunteer team.
Some of my volunteers got involved locally, which excited me! But they should have been included on the campaign trail, leaving some big shoes to fill.
Others made many promises, and big-money donors once again approached me. The catch was that once elected, I would have to promise them a lobbying position somewhere in D.C.
I told them that if they wanted to fund my campaign because they believed in me, great—but I'm not doing any special favors for money.
Long story short, I ran my campaign by myself for most of the race.
I was exhausted, overworked, burnt out, had zero help, and was on the verge of suspending my campaign in November 2023.
Remarkably, few people donated despite my asking for only $5, which does make a difference as it signals support.
Instead, most people complained on social media. Some would reach out to me and try to tell me what to do, but then they would refuse to donate so I could get it done.
I'm not sharing all of this to complain or gain sympathy—I'm sharing it to give some perspective on what it's like to be a grassroots candidate who lays everything on the line to stand and fight alone if necessary.
To this day, most people think we had money and a big team, but we did not.
I credit my cousin, Wes Virdell, who had a heart-to-heart with me in November - right before my wife and I went on Thanksgiving vacation - and encouraged me to think through my next steps.
I took those ten days to unplug, step away from politics, recharge, and figure out if I wanted to continue this fight.
I chose and forged ahead despite having little to no help on my campaign.
Then, one of my volunteers from 2022 reached out and learned of the situation and immediately sprung into action...
That person was Sarah Dolan, who became my Coalition Director.
Throughout the rest of the race, she and I ran our campaign.
And in February, a lot more people began to step up.
We received feedback from people who said they didn't see our signs in their neighborhood or at the polls. Unfortunately, our resources only allowed us to purchase fifty large 4x8 and five hundred yard signs.
Additionally, we had reports that some who requested signs had not received them. This situation happened because Sarah and I were the only ones hand-delivering them.
Had we had more resources available, we could've ordered more signs, rallied more volunteers, created jobs by hiring people to help, and sent out mailers—which cost about **$40,000 per mailout**.
We had an elected official in Montgomery County show support to my face while actively working against me behind the scenes. We also believe this person was responsible for blocking Paxton's and Trump's endorsements.
There was an organization in Montgomery County that claimed to support me but wouldn't endorse me because they didn't believe I was a viable candidate (I guess they're eating those words now). Thankfully, General Flynn, Mattress Mack, Michael Berry, Montgomery County Tea Party, Montgomery County Freedom Caucus, Texans for Vaccine Choice, Chad Prather, Dr. Hotze, Latinos for America First, and the Conservative Coalition of Harris County all saw me as a viable candidate.
Rumors about my family were spread in East County, and they were **absolute lies** \- rumors that could destroy a family and the reputations of good people.
I share all of this because I'm not doing this for applause, money, or to get rich - I put myself through all this for **you**!
**Let me be reiterate...**
I am not a well-funded, well-connected politician seeking more power and influence. I am a working-class, self-employed small business owner and constituent of this district. As someone who has experienced firsthand the struggles and challenges of everyday Americans, I ran for Congress to bring a fresh perspective and fight for the people who have been misrepresented.
I am a candidate who truly believes in enforcing the rule of law, limiting the government, and bringing accountability back to Congress.
I know that our government is ignoring us.
I also don't just sit on the sidelines or complain on social media.
I take action.
**You** are worth it!
**TEXAS** is worth it!
And **AMERICA** is worth it!
We raised less than **$30k** and took over 40% of the votes, keeping Crenshaw under 60%.
To put that into perspective, we spent roughly $1 per vote, while Crenshaw spent approximately $74.
These results mean that if we had raised another $15-20k, it would have pushed us over the edge to victory.
Never think your $1, $5, or $10 donation doesn't count.
I work for YOU, not the bureaucratic special interests in Washington, D.C.
So, from the bottom of my heart, I thank every one of you for your confidence in and support of our campaign.
_**The Future**_
Keep your signs... 2026 will be here before you know it!
**If you truly support me for 2026** , I'm asking you to donate a recurring $5 or $10 per month--don't forget to tick the highlighted checkbox marking it a monthly recurring donation.
We cannot allow a lack of resources to once again be our downfall.
**Click here:** [https://secure.anedot.com/jamesonellisforcongress/donate](https://jamesonellis.lt.acemlna.com/Prod/link-tracker?redirectUrl=aHR0cHMlM0ElMkYlMkZzZWN1cmUuYW5lZG90LmNvbSUyRmphbWVzb25lbGxpc2ZvcmNvbmdyZXNzJTJGZG9uYXRl&sig=4GKKrpBusNBrxGL2a6qnYfjuftnAjcdbEhXxJ7j5mwr8&iat=1710763423&a=%7C%7C611311006%7C%7C&account=jamesonellis%2Eactivehosted%2Ecom&email=yzS%2Fz67mNgrHA8zfL5dYEJmFuHWUl2AZbVd37Xd%2Frd0%2FUlPZ%3A8JoDXx2vScYQ5NWgbx3wbeBJ4dxqjyeE&s=cabcbe31a720242486b887158a77876f&i=238A276A1A2156)

Friend
Did you hear the news? Congressman Jack Bergman is on Team Hudson.
---
| I am extremely honored and privileged to receive the backing of Congressman Bergman, whose family roots stretch back to the 1800's when Jack's ancestors were Upper Peninsula iron miners.
Honored ... because this support comes from the highest ranking combat veteran to have ever served in the U.S. House and because I can think of no Member of Congress who works harder than Jack Bergman, serving on both the Veterans Affairs and Armed Services committees.
And, I'm privileged ... because as the challenger in this campaign, I am very grateful in a competitive Republican primary to receive this respected congressman's support..
---
| "In these crazy times, we can use more people in Congress who have Paul's common sense as well as his deep understanding of the US Constitution."
\- U.S. Rep. Jack Bergman

Hiring staff, recruiting and training volunteers, equipping them with the very best technology to identify our voter and secure their vote by November 5th. There's no time to lose. In closing, I can't help but think how Adam Schiff and his team of high-priced DC consultants thought they were being savvy in trying to make sure I became their opponent in General Election. Reports are they even spent money running ads promoting me. But what they've really done is awaken a sleeping giant here. It was a place where a scrawny little kid could start as a bat boy for his heroes, work hard, win a World Series, and land on a Topps baseball card. California can be that place again. America can be that place again. And it starts with throwing out political liars and connivers like Adam Schiff and reclaiming our freedom roots. Time is the most important factor. Thank you!

## U.S., SpaceX Building Spy Satellite Network
Elon Musk's SpaceX is building [a network of hundreds of spy satellites](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJxskL2SqzAUg5_GdIfxX4AUFLehy223ZIw5hrMxNmObsLz9TlJvpZHUSN_XY3wY8hSW_2bDvrg4GlvohaMC0YHUo67m3iFKVBX2ohW8bbq7ENXac4EGdefQTTeljb41k1RqErNFrriYKuoll5or0fH7rVFdzUXbNndjnNPSINdMc5ypxFR_RwplReev-MJU27hVvl9L2TNT_5gcmBzO86wTHgVTfvdMDgXtGqKPy8XkkHdjkclhO_Izw8f9AGWYDvIzhQXyfkE2Bb2nghCwnDE94chA4RMuGCyCecsFOR7JYob3AeAKRMPkUKV-3k_ynnLTMs2XzZD_bC1_kvsNAAD__4RacfE) for U.S. intelligence agencies, according to sources familiar with the program. SpaceX's Starshield division is launching the network under a $1.8 billion contract signed in 2021 with the National Reconnaissance Office, which oversees spy satellites. The program underlines the deepening ties between SpaceX and the U.S. government. The low earth-orbiting satellite system [would support ground forces](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJxs0L3uozAQBPCnMd2itXH4KCiuocu1VyLHXmAvxka2CZe3PyX1v5riJ41G8-c-3w17Dutvs9NYljgbW_hFcwOyB6VnXblxIVLUVDTKTmLX9oOU1TZKifqmnVKDI7tovClEJy0iNtI-yFY8KlQaG9njcGubvkbZde1gzLJoZQi10EiOS0z138ihbLT4d3xRqm3cKz9upRxZNL-EmoSaruuqbXjYDwo1faqFmrARapKtUNN-5meGfBhL_4AzPE72jsMK-XhDNoW850IQqFwxPWGJCc4MHL6wUrAE5hNvyPFMljKU6B0kOgulXG9l91Ua3XGx95zbTmhcd8P-O7b8eN3_AAAA__8HVXF8) and help the military quickly spot potential targets worldwide.
## Hertz CEO Resigns After Electric Car Fiasco
Hertz CEO Stephen Scherr [resigned this weekend](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJxskLGO4yAUAL8Gd1jwzGFTUCSFdU2uvdJ6dh6GXRssILGyX7_K1tvONKP5f5tuGLYQ13-4k60uTbjU8KSp43LgoCbV3K0jAuoasrKXoteDkbLxdtGaEGh22gxCzEYZVGBQDA6k0_3cBAsClOjkIMwf3Q2tkH2vDaJzCpCEYkrQPdSU248UYvXktld6Um6XtDeb9bUehXUXBiOD8TzPdi_x7RiMFPmjMBj3FOnFYFzSfmAM9Gaecv3iCyVeKh2eIi-Lp5x5phLWWDi6SpnTkx-P4vmaqPD5USqDETO_XuUnXNTfJtv7cYZtC0X3TIl1x7D9lNVfP30HAAD__8Otang) in the wake of the company's losses from investing heavily in electric vehicles. Last month, Hertz announced its biggest quarterly operating loss since 2020, going from a profit of $464 million to a loss of $348 million. The rental car company invested heavily in an electric car rental fleet that was [too expensive to maintain](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJxs0L1uKyEQQOGngQ6LAcxPQXEbd75tyhVmZ81EeHEAbRQ_fZTUaU9zpO_tulwTVdrv_9MD49zakvKkAxctwAtlFsPXuCEq1BwjOJDO-gDAS7TrOQTvFJistfPGAgSd11uCmwaFjlNUUhmpwctwttqfJDhnQ0rbZlRCaZiRuNJs_fTeaJ8Ft_rVDuyn3B68xjLnczD9j6kLU5eP109m6lKwz5fI2MSY-Cy4i5EL9i46DrrvQ-AhsGKenbI4sFCuOAT4M2gD3gfe4_r8pFppWMeMvD8S1d_l_BPgOwAA__-zpluv) and had a lower resale value than expected. The company dropped 20,000 EVs, about a third of its electric fleet. Scherr, who led Hertz for two years, will step down on March 31 and be replaced by Gil West, former Chief Operating Officer of Delta Airlines.

name: Becky Wagner
subject: There’s no doubt my husband made the right decision
body:
Dear Friend,

They're trying to ruin a great man...

Between the anger and tears, that's what keeps going through my mind when I think about the unfair attacks on my hero police officer husband, Mark Wagner, as his trial date quickly approaches on March 18th.
[](https://links.conservativesgive.com/u/click?_t=959d0fa54cad47baa4213176314ae733&_m=8fc2d5c24e644fd4bb6548c41cc5179b&_e=bwHN5P7P5amUzt4BeSG7htJseviVEWsE5SIumg2SfcINddn12eREz2UG4pVh6eey9prUsSRTatucIu7pTDVJvoUKRQZpvBCjdpirM7Bm9bQOITxWggufmA2YVcfsmrGCOm6gttNIGNbv81cfZjioPpDmS8FPp34Z5hMAyIXipl_q2auzYXibSLON9oEiM7tyi3zrrY8VNWATj0kay5sjFS6RlG6OrkDP_5GOa-VRacItswjNgiGdtS1_jbYR1rEBfUzeWVctmfeVgx_cVEinYh7McdlDGiHlOelQpZeSxym2MdRNPfZbvaqAUlauC0ZCWRpMoi1hukedNDSk_KQx7ErTROBWu4XDMVkPm9fPNIQ%3D)
That's Mark in the picture I sent you, along with our boys Nolan and Jacob and dog Kilo.

Not only is Mark a highly respected officer, he's an incredibly supportive father, a loving husband, and a fierce friend.

But Mark worked in far-Left Madison, Wisconsin - and the "defund the police" mob whipped up rage and smeared Mark as a racist. The corrupt media repeatedly LIED about Mark to trash his reputation.

Now Mark faces 10 YEARS behind bars for doing exactly what he was trained to do in the line of duty - and I'm scared I might lose him. **[That's why I wrote this letter to you, someone I've never met before, to ask for your help.](https://links.conservativesgive.com/u/click?_t=959d0fa54cad47baa4213176314ae733&_m=8fc2d5c24e644fd4bb6548c41cc5179b&_e=bwHN5P7P5amUzt4BeSG7htJseviVEWsE5SIumg2SfcINddn12eREz2UG4pVh6eey9prUsSRTatucIu7pTDVJvoUKRQZpvBCjdpirM7Bm9bQOITxWggufmA2YVcfsmrGCOm6gttNIGNbv81cfZjioPpDmS8FPp34Z5hMAyIXipl_q2auzYXibSLON9oEiM7tyi3zrrY8VNWATj0kay5sjFWg1yNPkCjTHzzaL4sLlu0UDa3H1IEMcI4neLVJHZrNlKjsKTaN06fk8UOMQ3YQc5Md7NGBVd9PERTGmWozawqFEfAR-a-uJiIGOSzCZRTSYPs4kPxkBLjn-8AmOJW2TFtPQan4EpOBgHIneYuqcE1U%3D)**

But first, please let me explain what happened...

On the morning of February 3, 2022, Mark and other officers tried to arrest a _violent_ _criminal_ named Quadren Wilson.

Wilson has a rap sheet a mile long with dozens of arrests for drug distribution, theft, witness intimidation, battery, eluding police, and more. He was wanted for dealing fentanyl to a man found dead in a restaurant bathroom.

Mark's arrest team had a plan in place to capture the suspect in his vehicle. So they pulled in their trucks to block his car on both ends. But he floored the accelerator, spinning his wheels wildly in a desperate attempt to escape.

My husband and another officer exited their vehicle. Mark was holding one of those big POLICE shields and had his gun drawn. But the suspect refused Mark's commands to show his hands.

With the wheels screeching and smoking, Mark and the other officer saw the suspect reach into the center console and pull his hand up.

Mark thought the suspect had a gun. He heard what he thought was gunfire and felt something hit his shield and push him backward.

**Both Mark and the other officer responded to this life-threatening situation by firing into the vehicle.**

Thankfully, the suspect survived and no one else was injured. But because he is black and Mark is white - anti-police radicals jumped at the chance to target my husband.

Protesters drummed up a racial firestorm by spreading lies that the suspect "had his hands up" and that he "was shot five times in the back." The corrupt liberal media repeated these lies and painted my husband as a monster.

Then on September 22, 2022, the liberal District Attorney caved to the mob and filed BOGUS felony charges against Mark. **Now Mark faces 10 YEARS in prison. His trial is scheduled to begin on March 18th.**

**[Now I hope you can see why I'm turning to you for help today.](https://links.conservativesgive.com/u/click?_t=959d0fa54cad47baa4213176314ae733&_m=8fc2d5c24e644fd4bb6548c41cc5179b&_e=bwHN5P7P5amUzt4BeSG7htJseviVEWsE5SIumg2SfcINddn12eREz2UG4pVh6eey9prUsSRTatucIu7pTDVJvoUKRQZpvBCjdpirM7Bm9bQOITxWggufmA2YVcfsmrGCOm6gttNIGNbv81cfZjioPpDmS8FPp34Z5hMAyIXipl_q2auzYXibSLON9oEiM7tyi3zrrY8VNWATj0kay5sjFaSin5qANnG1Lz80QA8Q8NfIvGzjreRZ2fjd3ENBp_E-h0IvuNf4vNZXsSADJs0b3RvinpaRcGHM6dw6fdKr4_MwkhTyngc9FjUOXfb9145TjzWm5o8aEEk5DNCxCCBRBc3VBmQDlyTBmC9D3Acct9o%3D)**

Mark dedicated his life to helping others. He's spent 30 years in law enforcement, most of them with the Milwaukee Police Department (MPD).

We knew fighting alone against the anti-police movement here in Wisconsin would be impossible and our hope that justice would prevail was quickly fading when we received a call from **the Law Enforcement Legal Defense Fund (LELDF)** offering to help Mark.

This incredible organization helps innocent officers, like my husband, who have been unfairly prosecuted for split-second, use-of-force decisions in the line of duty.

Law and justice experts like President Ronald Reagan's Attorney General Edwin Meese and former FBI Assistant Director Ronald Hosko serve on LELDF's Board. LELDF's president, Jason Johnson, served over 20 years as a police officer, including as Deputy Commissioner of the Baltimore Police Department.

In short, these are experts when it comes to policing. And they thoroughly vet cases to determine if an officer was wrongly accused or charged before deciding to help.

They provide legal counsel, expert witnesses, whatever is needed to make sure wrongly accused police officers get a fair shake in court. And they do it all free of charge!

But LELDF doesn't receive any money from the government to help police officers facing unjust charges. They're funded entirely by the generous support of folks like you who can recognize a miscarriage of justice and want to help fix it.

Now I must ask if you're one of those people...

**[Will you please help my husband Mark fight to clear his name by rushing a generous, tax-deductible donation to LELDF today?](https://links.conservativesgive.com/u/click?_t=959d0fa54cad47baa4213176314ae733&_m=8fc2d5c24e644fd4bb6548c41cc5179b&_e=bwHN5P7P5amUzt4BeSG7htJseviVEWsE5SIumg2SfcINddn12eREz2UG4pVh6eey9prUsSRTatucIu7pTDVJvoUKRQZpvBCjdpirM7Bm9bQOITxWggufmA2YVcfsmrGCOm6gttNIGNbv81cfZjioPpDmS8FPp34Z5hMAyIXipl_q2auzYXibSLON9oEiM7tyi3zrrY8VNWATj0kay5sjFZiFGoxO0k05cdDBQpadZPwUt0VkSbgBrE5hTUg0CvyDDGJQI8kDcjG8YH5rW4hR29eMzU9Oj2JmZgNaX070RqS_PdOdpX2CF7L2Q2Ju6QYqRNW5C7ReufAATA8Y3ZklcKiEDCHOMHWI3c6g3uYMe1o%3D)**

Your kind gift today of $35, $50, or $100 to help Mark will mean so much to my family.

Or, if you're blessed with the means to help with a gift of $250, $500, or even $1,000 or more, I pray you will so my husband doesn't spend the next 10 YEARS behind bars away from our family.

With the trial just around the corner, there is no time to waste. **[So please follow this link to make your tax-deductible donation right away.](https://links.conservativesgive.com/u/click?_t=959d0fa54cad47baa4213176314ae733&_m=8fc2d5c24e644fd4bb6548c41cc5179b&_e=bwHN5P7P5amUzt4BeSG7htJseviVEWsE5SIumg2SfcINddn12eREz2UG4pVh6eey9prUsSRTatucIu7pTDVJvoUKRQZpvBCjdpirM7Bm9bQOITxWggufmA2YVcfsmrGCOm6gttNIGNbv81cfZjioPpDmS8FPp34Z5hMAyIXipl_q2auzYXibSLON9oEiM7tyi3zrrY8VNWATj0kay5sjFd80J5rtzez1XcN6ru86rAEzprD9kVGLYdUlkBQa-MJ5hYj64NuJRfzqifWLMvKzeu_Yz7QIk37oTu4ZVadqFnuDwPCQosx6Et2Z4Dn69bTeIoqHeaFPHuA3zJLuZUIhotdJx2wkSb7Enu0U6t951Kw%3D)**

Any gift amount you can give today is truly a blessing. No matter what, please say a prayer for Mark and our family.

Thank you in advance for your generous support of my family and LELDF.

With deepest gratitude,
Becky Wagner

that's why I'm running for Senate.

hungry for change, and if you and I work together to reach voters

When we
win here... when we rip this seat out the hands of the radical

...we
start the nationwide Republican Comeback Rally our country
desperately needs.
Thank you
and God Bless,

Steve

| Hello All,
Thank you for your tremendous support during the recent campaign for State Committee! Now that the election has concluded, my Campaign Manager Amanda Orlando and I, want to take this opportunity to correct the record about false claims made about me, personally, and our campaign for Governor over the last few months.
In 2023, the Office of Campaign and Political Finance (OCPF) conducted regular audits of state-wide campaigns that had concluded, including the "Diehl for Governor" committee. OCPF also audited MassGOP. In their review, OCPF identified some MassGOP expenditures which they required to be listed as "in-kind" donations to the Diehl campaign.
One of those payments was $1,000 from the MassGOP to the Howie Carr Show in the fall of 2022, for radio ads regarding Maura Healey's "America is Burning" comment. In December of 2023, the party and OCPF advised us that the Diehl committee needed to amend the 2022 report to reflect it as an in-kind donation. On a recent show, Howie has claimed that I owed him money, which is patently false. We amended our report as instructed on 1/22/2024 with the full knowledge and approval of the current chair, Amy Carnevale, and John Milligan, her Executive Director.
Further, in 2022, Mittcom was hired as a vendor, by the MassGOP, to produce and run TV and radio ads to promote policy positions that would benefit Republican candidates. Currently, Mittcom is suing the MassGOP for overdue payments. Despite claims brought by individuals that this debt was incurred by the Diehl committee, it was not. In fact, no member of the Diehl committee, nor the Committee itself, has been named as a defendant in that lawsuit.
Ironically, during the OCPF audits, we DID find that a number of donors to the Diehl committee had contributed more than the allowable, annual limit. A combination of data entry errors and misinterpretations by our compliance firm (hired to make sure state law was followed) have created a situation in which we need to reimburse a handful of individual donors for what they gave over the limit.
As we move forward in 2024, I'll be raising funds into the campaign account so that we can ensure that all problems identified by OCPF are remediated and our reports are updated.
I've always prided myself on being honest and forthright with my supporters, the voters, and the press. If you're willing to help, you can make a campaign contribution here: [https://secure.winred.com/diehl-committee/donate-today](https://r20.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001y0oYJbHRoNQ5_6Go5RG_jRk15sSDlb_6QgH-i8Kaf-yufh5-A8ohqB7jrPLwDyKtOMcCXvCiqTWbWxOCRZmAhRsresn79ISGzt3NnMnsL1kdOo62-5pYvjXXFeyZtT-T1RRRNbRVYSQaRxjmJclO9cJSIw5ldLLclpBJyi0GCewKpdpL22u-VkXC3-MSsuKn&c=lj2QyoagVI2IsRkKffIf7mJsu4zFYJrCl0jJn6GMLlj65a25whYiOg==&ch=-Y5fo0pVCud01BukEixdcoxIiIB-qbb2tBbFaKEKtGL587BYgFrUzA==)
I am also considering a run for State Senate to work on the difficult issues facing the Commonwealth right now. Stay tuned for more information related to that potential campaign!

clean_body: | | | | == | Hello All, Thank you for your tremendous support during the recent campaign for State Committee! Now that the election has concluded, my Campaign Manager Amanda Orlando and I, want to take this opportunity to correct the record about false claims made about me, personally, and our campaign for Governor over the last few months. In 2023, the Office of Campaign and Political Finance (OCPF) conducted regular audits of state-wide campaigns that had concluded, including the "Diehl for Governor" committee. OCPF also audited MassGOP. In their review, OCPF identified some MassGOP expenditures which they required to be listed as "in-kind" donations to the Diehl campaign. One of those payments was $1,000 from the MassGOP to the Howie Carr Show in the fall of 2022, for radio ads regarding Maura Healey's "America is Burning" comment. In December of 2023, the party and OCPF advised us that the Diehl committee needed to amend the 2022 report to reflect it as an in-kind donation. On a recent show, Howie has claimed that I owed him money, which is patently false. We amended our report as instructed on 1/22/2024 with the full knowledge and approval of the current chair, Amy Carnevale, and John Milligan, her Executive Director. Further, in 2022, Mittcom was hired as a vendor, by the MassGOP, to produce and run TV and radio ads to promote policy positions that would benefit Republican candidates. Currently, Mittcom is suing the MassGOP for overdue payments. Despite claims brought by individuals that this debt was incurred by the Diehl committee, it was not. In fact, no member of the Diehl committee, nor the Committee itself, has been named as a defendant in that lawsuit. Ironically, during the OCPF audits, we DID find that a number of donors to the Diehl committee had contributed more than the allowable, annual limit. A combination of data entry errors and misinterpretations by our compliance firm (hired to make sure state law was followed) have created a situation in which we need to reimburse a handful of individual donors for what they gave over the limit. As we move forward in 2024, I'll be raising funds into the campaign account so that we can ensure that all problems identified by OCPF are remediated and our reports are updated. I've always prided myself on being honest and forthright with my supporters, the voters, and the press. If you're willing to help, you can make a campaign contribution here: == I am also considering a run for State Senate to work on the difficult issues facing the Commonwealth right now. Stay tuned for more information related to that potential campaign! | Friends, Do you remember all of the shenanigans that took place this past June when I ran for re-election to the Virginia Senate?
It all took place under the leadership of GOP Chair Leslie Haley. This Tuesday is our chance to replace her as Chesterfield GOP Chair with an honest, principled Constitutional patriot, Dee Dee Van Buren.
I'm asking you to get out and vote for Dee Dee Van Buren and the "Re-unify the Red" slate of candidates running for GOP executive leadership in Chesterfield.
Aren't you sick and tired of the "keep it small, keep it all" good old boy and girl GOP leadership in Chesterfield, that doesn't represent most of you who vote Republican?
Sadly, the Chesterfield GOP leadership has become an exclusive bunch of elitists who put their finger on the scale for RINO candidates elected and actively work against MAGA and true conservative candidates. This has to stop.
We need a chair who has a history of strong support for President Donald J Trump and will give it everything they have to ensure he is elected this coming November.
That won't happen under current leadership.
Please tell all of your friends who live in Chesterfield to get out and vote tomorrow, Tuesday, March 19. Notice the current establishment GOP has only given you 2 hours to vote in one location. That's by design.
They don't want you to vote. They want to make it inconvenient for you to vote, so that you won't and they can stay in power and control who can run for office.
We need to replace them. And now is our chance.
We need fresh new leadership in the Chesterfield GOP, which is why I encourage all conservatives and Republicans living in Chesterfield to get out and vote for the: "RE-UNIFY THE RED" slate of candidates this coming Tuesday, March 19 between the hours of 5:30pm and 7:30pm at Swift Creek Middle School. It will only take a few minutes to vote and you don't need to stay.
Rumor is that the establishment GOP old guard is going to get their people out early so that there is a long line and you won't stay to vote.
So get there early. And be determined to vote, no matter what they try to pull.
You don't need to be a member of the Chesterfield GOP to vote. Tell every Republican you know who lives in Chesterfield to get out and vote for the Re-unify the Red slate.
I am confident that Dee Dee Van Buren and the "Re-unify the Red" slate will bring all Republicans together, work hard to elect Donald J Trump this November, and will actively work to grow the current membership of the Chesterfield GOP, so that we can ensure Chesterfield County stays "red."
Be determined to vote tomorrow and call everyone you know who lives in Chesterfield to turn out and vote so that we can make the Chesterfield GOP great again.

body:
Smash it over the fence

| | | [](http://e.1600daily.com/rd/9z2zjqmdcpc5q1nnqlpu6dpt7687f79pift58qf29k8_rp22sh2s8i6ep30ctjmeor6cph2bs)

---
| | Friend, I've played in lots of double-headers. And that's exactly what you and I have on our hands here. A one-on-one matchup with Adam Schiff on November 5th. **[**Can I count on your contribution of $6 to help defeat Adam Schiff today?**](http://e.1600daily.com/rd/9z2zei40ku60i70ogd776p6bhuuimq5soqvk87enono_rp22sh2s8i6ep30ctjmeor6cph2bs)** You see, Adam Schiff's enablers in the corporate media are already spreading the lie that this race is over. They're saying you and I don't have a chance (just like they did when I entered the race back in October). They're saying that Adam Schiff notched a double victory by advancing to the General Election and drawing me as his opponent. In other words, they're ready, willing and able to cut California voters entirely out of the picture again. My response to Schiff's allies saying they'd rather face me: **_Be careful what you wish for._** I'd liken this to my playing days when a cocky opposing pitcher throws a 94mph fastball right over the plate. I'll tell you, the ball would look as big as a grapefruit before I'd smash it over the fence and touch all the bases on the way home. And look how far we've already made it. I'm in first place in the primary and gaining momentum headed towards the November election. Look, I'm not saying this will be easy. Quite the opposite. It's going to be a nonstop, 58-county fight between now and November 5th. **[That said, I must ask: will you rush a contribution to my senate campaign today?](http://e.1600daily.com/rd/9z2zo2ib0bmtpnp4rovtsrqp1scltsutmd9ljmisb0o_rp22sh2s8i6ep30ctjmeor6cph2bs) ** This is going to be an expensive fight. Hiring staff, recruiting and training volunteers, equipping them with the very best technology to identify our voter and secure their vote by November 5th. There's no time to lose. In closing, I can't help but think how Adam Schiff and his team of high-priced DC consultants thought they were being savvy in trying to make sure I became their opponent in General Election. Reports are they even spent money running ads promoting me. But what they've really done is awaken a sleeping giant here. Remember, before it became a wasteland of crime, homelessness, and sky-high taxes, California was a land of dreamers, a land of opportunity. It was a place where a scrawny little kid could start as a bat boy for his heroes, work hard, win a World Series, and land on a Topps baseball card. California can be that place again. America can be that place again. And it starts with throwing out political liars and connivers like Adam Schiff and reclaiming our freedom roots. Time is the most important factor. Thank you!
---

---

Make no mistake, while his cash advantage is greatly diminished, as I write these words, Adam Schiff, Nancy Pelosi, and Chuck Schumer are quickly reloading. The ActBlue political machine has the capacity to pump millions into his race in the blink of an eye. You and I cannot give them any daylight. **[**Your prompt support is critical.**](http://e.1600daily.com/rd/9z2zpf445gsgebsgdq0cesl5op5qbi7a40il0iskf3g_rp22sh2s8i6ep30ctjmeor6cph2bs)** Please don't delay.

Democrats continue to bray that democracy is on the ballot in November, even though it was lost long ago. With [bipartisan support](https://substack.com/redirect/2c1f153f-731c-4c9f-9b48-4b107ba86291?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) enabling authoritarianism and human rights abuses [from our nation's borders to Gaza](https://substack.com/redirect/15d95ffe-5c70-4af9-89c4-b4c5ef484526?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), it is farcical to claim that America respects democracy in any meaningful sense.
Washington not only disrespects human rights and international law, but also ignores the will of its own citizens embodied in elections. Concerns about elections being effectively rigged--whether by political party elites, the national security apparatus, or the press--find ample grounds for justification, but tend to overlook attacks on voting rights as a separate threat to election integrity
Around the time that the Supreme Court struck down _Roe v. Wade_ , Americans finally started paying attention to the crisis in the judiciary that has been festering for at least the last generation.
Having dedicated an earlier part of my career to defending the courts from a right wing takeover that has grown entrenched despite my better efforts, I wanted to take a few minutes to explain the most recent example of judicial demagoguery, how it has degraded democracy, and how it is poised to grow even worse.
### **Law v. politics**
Since the earliest days of the Republic, political scientists, policymakers, and judges alike have all recognized the inherent tension between law and politics.
The political process is designed to be majoritarian. It is a process designed to aggregate public perspectives, and theoretically inform the actions of government based on the consent of the governed.
In sharp contrast, law is designed to be counter-majoritarian. It necessarily involves elite appointed figures (judges) making decisions without popular input, often to overturn the actions of majoritarian political branches like Congress.
That tension is one reason why judges have historically practiced judicial restraint, and pilloried each other, when stepping beyond their roles, with charges of judicial activism. While conservative critics labeled the judges of the Warren Court as activists, the far greater example of judicial activism has been the relentless war on civil rights by the Supreme Court majorities led by William Rehnquist and his protege, John Roberts.
_Help inform your friends!_
[ Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=1018597&post_id=142705952&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTQyNzA1OTUyLCJpYXQiOjE3MTA3NjUxODUsImV4cCI6MTcxMzM1NzE4NSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTEwMTg1OTciLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.JvZ5AupTQ5hMPp3rYWhc7iZcceAouxofyu5dsQOF6JM)
### **Section 5 's pre-clearance provisions**
In 2013, the Roberts Court struck down critical provisions of the Voting Rights Act, which was first enacted in 1965 and most recently re-authorized in 2006 under [remarkable circumstances](https://substack.com/redirect/6360af72-0eaf-4259-bb52-1fd0781f62d6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The VRA was re-authorized not only by an overwhelming bipartisan majority in the House, but also a (rare) unanimous vote in the Senate before being signed into law by President George W. Bush.
The VRA was enacted in order to remedy a legacy of racial discrimination, particularly in the South. Its passage was a central victory of the civil rights movement, which (contrary to popular belief) [was denied most of its goals](https://substack.com/redirect/70ef7717-2480-4cc1-80c3-af828beb2000?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), while being offered procedural voting rights as something of a concession.
When President Lyndon Johnson signed the Civil Rights Act of 1965, [he knew](https://substack.com/redirect/4e4d5d7d-75dd-4be4-b71a-5808b56b61af?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that his party would lose the South for a generation. The only thing he was wrong about was that the dedication of the South to the GOP would frankly last even longer.
One of the VRA's most critical provisions was Section 5, which allowed the Justice Department to require jurisdictions with a history of racial discrimination to pre-clear changes to their voting laws to make sure that they didn't undermine civil rights _before_ any proposed changes took effect. That provision in the law gave the Justice Department a crucial administrative role as an overseer of local jurisdictions and states that refused to heed the rights of their citizens.
Before it was neutralized, Section 5 stopped local, county, and state governments from retrogression, ensuring that progress in voting rights would not be lost to racial majorities eager to entrench their own power. It particularly prevented jurisdictions from taking steps that marginalize minority voters, like purging registration lists or changing the locations of voting sites without adequate public notice.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/56020c31-4b00-4849-80dc-2819094c5a4a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
While the Roberts Court's decision in _[Shelby County v. Holder](https://substack.com/redirect/d138a135-7c30-47b9-a623-a06492a73d1a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[ (2013)](https://substack.com/redirect/d138a135-7c30-47b9-a623-a06492a73d1a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) did not formally strike down Section 5, it rendered it unenforceable by striking down the coverage formula in Section 4(b). The Court imagined that racial discrimination in the South was a thing of the past, but by hamstringing the VRA's pre-clearance provisions, the Justices effectively invited its escalation. Congress could theoretically muster a majority to update the coverage formula, as the Court suggested in _Shelby County_ , but that's not likely to happen anytime soon given the partisan rancor that prevents Members from agreeing on much beyond [bipartisan weapons sales](https://substack.com/redirect/0f578a27-839a-4a60-8149-e87751e59e7d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
When the Supreme Court rendered Section 5 effectively unenforceable, some observers suggested that the VRA still had teeth because Section 2 survived. Section 2 is a parallel section allowing private parties to enforce the law after the fact, separate from the Justice Department's authority under Section 5 to pre-clear--or block--changes to voting laws before they were implemented.
Sadly, assurances that communities could continue to rely on Section 2 appear to have been misplaced.

### **Section 2 's private right of action**
Reflecting the influence of Trump-appointed judges on the law, Justice Neil Gorsuch suggested in 2021 that the private parties do not enjoy a private right of action under Section 2 of the VRA. While his opinion in _[Brnovich v. DNC (2021)](https://substack.com/redirect/0690aecf-daab-4e6b-9f13-e8b04ef08d1f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ did not carry the force of law, it effectively invited any number of judges in the lower courts to set up a case giving Gorsuch a chance to bake his once fringe opinion into the law.
That process is well underway.
In 2022, Judge Lee Rudofsky (who former President Trump appointed to the bench in 2019) took the invitation issued by Justice Gorsuch the year before, ruling in _[NAACP v. Arkansas Board of Apportionment](https://substack.com/redirect/c2f8109a-f1f6-46c5-810d-f718d18ae9ae?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ that private plaintiffs lack standing to enforce Section 2. His ruling was upheld 2-1 by a three-judge panel of the 8th Circuit Court of Appeals, even though it would effectively neutralize the last remaining vestige of the VRA's once formidable attempt to end racial discrimination in voting.
The case is now pending before the Supreme Court, whose decision could hold monumental implications for voting rights. Over the course of the past 40 years, [over 96%](https://substack.com/redirect/11ff9e1a-b4fb-425c-9f79-dc4ac56c822d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of the Section 2 cases filed in federal courts have been filed by private plaintiffs normally represented by non-profit organizations like the NAACP or ACLU. That entire line of cases would come to a screeching halt if the Supreme Court upholds Rudofsky's ruling.
### **What ethics?**
Beyond the crisis in democracy sparked by the right wing attack on the Voting Rights Act is a long-standing--and ongoing--scandal with respect to judicial ethics.
Because judges operate in an inherently anti-democratic fashion by imposing elite judgments on the wheel of political majorities, the vast majority of them are required to recuse themselves from cases in which their interests are implicated. That's not a complicated rule, and it should not be controversial.
But while judges throughout the lower courts are effectively constrained by ethical principles, justices of the Supreme Court answer to no higher authority. They also seem to stoop to no lower standards.
Justice Thomas has made a [mockery](https://substack.com/redirect/3ba0d9e9-4dd9-4806-9d6d-c617f58dd757?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of judicial ethics by accepting lavish gifts from robber barons and magnets whose companies appear before his court. Justices Alito, Gorsuch, Kavanaugh, and Barrett [each lied](https://substack.com/redirect/2e261555-e28c-4782-97f1-cfe9c13f0db2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to Congress in order to secure their Senate confirmations. And Justice Kavanaugh appears to [embody](https://substack.com/redirect/049a588c-228f-43d7-b4b9-258098903d4a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the most distasteful aspects of predatory men.
After Senators [threatened](https://substack.com/redirect/b2fd0f54-efa2-41c7-92b8-1154efc6bfb8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to impose ethical reforms on the Court last year, the Justices of the Supreme Court [acknowledged](https://substack.com/redirect/91b80293-1623-424a-89dc-0e6b38c07359?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) these concerns by adopting a [new code of supposed ethics](https://substack.com/redirect/f0d55968-1968-4d68-a852-93855590b7d9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for the first time. But, as many observers have noted, [it has no teeth, plenty of loopholes](https://substack.com/redirect/4a2edf1b-0366-4429-8ef3-bc4ae72388a6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and should offer no comfort about the Court's political conflicts of interest.
Even though Supreme Court Justices remain effectively immune from any ethical restrictions, they wield more power than any elected member of government, enjoy lifetime tenure, and--at this moment--they hold a knife to the throat of whatever remains of democracy.
### **What this all means**
I've been vocal about the [evisceration](https://substack.com/redirect/2c1f153f-731c-4c9f-9b48-4b107ba86291?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of democracy in America, the [false hopes](https://substack.com/redirect/e01be966-26e4-40c4-a2ef-bb31709ec8e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that it could be redeemed in November, and particularly, the roles played by political parties and professional, [journalists](https://substack.com/redirect/022cb07d-6f09-4b0b-ab10-c6eb87a23033?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in enabling this escalating corruption. I've also recently written about the legitimate observation by a California Senate candidate that her race was effectively [rigged](https://substack.com/redirect/3c44b6de-b547-4ad9-bb71-a5105c4d4cf3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
This post highlights how the judiciary has also been mobilized to promote authoritarianism, degrade the ability of voters to impact government policy, and subject minority communities to arbitrary restraints on their ability to participate in elections.
America goes to great lengths to present itself to the world as a guardian of democracy. But our country's supposed commitment to democracy is ultimately a performance.

Escalating attacks on the Voting Rights Act have reduced elections in the U.S. to a charade | | | Mar 18| | | ∙| | Preview ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | | Democrats continue to bray that democracy is on the ballot in November, even though it was lost long ago. With enabling authoritarianism and human rights abuses , it is farcical to claim that America respects democracy in any meaningful sense. Washington not only disrespects human rights and international law, but also ignores the will of its own citizens embodied in elections. Concerns about elections being effectively rigged--whether by political party elites, the national security apparatus, or the press--find ample grounds for justification, but tend to overlook attacks on voting rights as a separate threat to election integrity Around the time that the Supreme Court struck down Roe v. Wade , Americans finally started paying attention to the crisis in the judiciary that has been festering for at least the last generation. Having dedicated an earlier part of my career to defending the courts from a right wing takeover that has grown entrenched despite my better efforts, I wanted to take a few minutes to explain the most recent example of judicial demagoguery, how it has degraded democracy, and how it is poised to grow even worse. Law v. politics Since the earliest days of the Republic, political scientists, policymakers, and judges alike have all recognized the inherent tension between law and politics. The political process is designed to be majoritarian. It is a process designed to aggregate public perspectives, and theoretically inform the actions of government based on the consent of the governed. In sharp contrast, law is designed to be counter-majoritarian. It necessarily involves elite appointed figures (judges) making decisions without popular input, often to overturn the actions of majoritarian political branches like Congress. That tension is one reason why judges have historically practiced judicial restraint, and pilloried each other, when stepping beyond their roles, with charges of judicial activism. While conservative critics labeled the judges of the Warren Court as activists, the far greater example of judicial activism has been the relentless war on civil rights by the Supreme Court majorities led by William Rehnquist and his protege, John Roberts. Help inform your friends! Section 5 's pre-clearance provisions In 2013, the Roberts Court struck down critical provisions of the Voting Rights Act, which was first enacted in 1965 and most recently re-authorized in 2006 under . The VRA was re-authorized not only by an overwhelming bipartisan majority in the House, but also a (rare) unanimous vote in the Senate before being signed into law by President George W. Bush. The VRA was enacted in order to remedy a legacy of racial discrimination, particularly in the South. Its passage was a central victory of the civil rights movement, which (contrary to popular belief) , while being offered procedural voting rights as something of a concession. When President Lyndon Johnson signed the Civil Rights Act of 1965, that his party would lose the South for a generation. The only thing he was wrong about was that the dedication of the South to the GOP would frankly last even longer. One of the VRA's most critical provisions was Section 5, which allowed the Justice Department to require jurisdictions with a history of racial discrimination to pre-clear changes to their voting laws to make sure that they didn't undermine civil rights before any proposed changes took effect. That provision in the law gave the Justice Department a crucial administrative role as an overseer of local jurisdictions and states that refused to heed the rights of their citizens. Before it was neutralized, Section 5 stopped local, county, and state governments from retrogression, ensuring that progress in voting rights would not be lost to racial majorities eager to entrench their own power. It particularly prevented jurisdictions from taking steps that marginalize minority voters, like purging registration lists or changing the locations of voting sites without adequate public notice. | | ---|---|--- While the Roberts Court's decision in did not formally strike down Section 5, it rendered it unenforceable by striking down the coverage formula in Section 4(b). The Court imagined that racial discrimination in the South was a thing of the past, but by hamstringing the VRA's pre-clearance provisions, the Justices effectively invited its escalation. Congress could theoretically muster a majority to update the coverage formula, as the Court suggested in Shelby County , but that's not likely to happen anytime soon given the partisan rancor that prevents Members from agreeing on much beyond . When the Supreme Court rendered Section 5 effectively unenforceable, some observers suggested that the VRA still had teeth because Section 2 survived. Section 2 is a parallel section allowing private parties to enforce the law after the fact, separate from the Justice Department's authority under Section 5 to pre-clear--or block--changes to voting laws before they were implemented. Sadly, assurances that communities could continue to rely on Section 2 appear to have been misplaced. You 're reading a publication supported by readers, rather than advertisers. To receive new posts, sign up for a free subscription! To support my work, consider becoming a paid subscriber. Section 2 's private right of action Reflecting the influence of Trump-appointed judges on the law, Justice Neil Gorsuch suggested in 2021 that the private parties do not enjoy a private right of action under Section 2 of the VRA. While his opinion in did not carry the force of law, it effectively invited any number of judges in the lower courts to set up a case giving Gorsuch a chance to bake his once fringe opinion into the law. That process is well underway. In 2022, Judge Lee Rudofsky (who former President Trump appointed to the bench in 2019) took the invitation issued by Justice Gorsuch the year before, ruling in that private plaintiffs lack standing to enforce Section 2. His ruling was upheld 2-1 by a three-judge panel of the 8th Circuit Court of Appeals, even though it would effectively neutralize the last remaining vestige of the VRA's once formidable attempt to end racial discrimination in voting. The case is now pending before the Supreme Court, whose decision could hold monumental implications for voting rights. Over the course of the past 40 years, of the Section 2 cases filed in federal courts have been filed by private plaintiffs normally represented by non-profit organizations like the NAACP or ACLU. That entire line of cases would come to a screeching halt if the Supreme Court upholds Rudofsky's ruling. What ethics? Beyond the crisis in democracy sparked by the right wing attack on the Voting Rights Act is a long-standing--and ongoing--scandal with respect to judicial ethics. Because judges operate in an inherently anti-democratic fashion by imposing elite judgments on the wheel of political majorities, the vast majority of them are required to recuse themselves from cases in which their interests are implicated. That's not a complicated rule, and it should not be controversial. But while judges throughout the lower courts are effectively constrained by ethical principles, justices of the Supreme Court answer to no higher authority. They also seem to stoop to no lower standards. Justice Thomas has made a of judicial ethics by accepting lavish gifts from robber barons and magnets whose companies appear before his court. Justices Alito, Gorsuch, Kavanaugh, and Barrett to Congress in order to secure their Senate confirmations. And Justice Kavanaugh appears to the most distasteful aspects of predatory men. After Senators to impose ethical reforms on the Court last year, the Justices of the Supreme Court these concerns by adopting a for the first time. But, as many observers have noted, , and should offer no comfort about the Court's political conflicts of interest. Even though Supreme Court Justices remain effectively immune from any ethical restrictions, they wield more power than any elected member of government, enjoy lifetime tenure, and--at this moment--they hold a knife to the throat of whatever remains of democracy. What this all means I've been vocal about the of democracy in America, the that it could be redeemed in November, and particularly, the roles played by political parties and professional, in enabling this escalating corruption. I've also recently written about the legitimate observation by a California Senate candidate that her race was effectively . This post highlights how the judiciary has also been mobilized to promote authoritarianism, degrade the ability of voters to impact government policy, and subject minority communities to arbitrary restraints on their ability to participate in elections. America goes to great lengths to present itself to the world as a guardian of democracy. But our country's supposed commitment to democracy is ultimately a performance. body:

---
Friends --
While I know our campaign sends a lot of emails your way, I want to take a few to tell you about my decision to run for Senate in the first place, and why your support is so important in our success.
The truth is, we all know America is _going through something_ right now. We seem to be living from crisis to crisis. But there are certain things that should be really simple:
Like living a middle-class life in the state that invented the middle class.
Like making things in America so that we’re in control of our own economic security.
Like protecting our children from the things that are _truly_ harming them.
And preserving our rights and our democracy so that our kids can live their version of the American dream.
**I’m running for Senate because I believe that we need a new generation of leaders that thinks differently, works harder, and never forgets the mission of public service.**
But my decision to run for Senate is also deeply personal to me, and it's related to what motivated me to first run for the House in 2018.
It's about my mom, Judy. She was diagnosed with stage IV ovarian cancer in 2009 — and didn't have health insurance at the time. She had let it lapse after the insurance companies had gouged her for years because she happened to have a pre-existing condition. She passed away in 2011, but that experience — of desperately trying to get her care at the same moment we were filling out bankruptcy paperwork — fueled me to run. I remember the exact moment that made me run: when the then-GOP controlled House of Representatives, the body I now serve in, voted to repeal those protections for people with pre-existing conditions.
Seven years later, the Republican leaders, fueled by the extreme wing of the party, are continuing the march to repeal things that the average Americans want. They want to privatize Social Security and Medicare, repeal drug price protections like allowing Medicare to negotiate, then there’s the rights they’re obsessed with repealing: a woman’s right to choose, voting rights, and any possible gun safety legislation.
By winning this Senate seat, we’ll help ensure that Democrats retain the (slight!) majority and can pass legislation that expands access to healthcare. Not the obsession with taking things away.
To be upfront: **Winning this race is going to take a lot of resources. A crazy amount. And we have to do it without raising a single dollar from corporate PACs.**
Donations this November – when we’re in the home stretch – are important. But donations now are even more important, because they allow us to map out a strategic plan and make decisions about when and how we reach voters.
[**That is why I would love it if you would consider donating $3 or whatever you can to my campaign today.](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/9?c0=ebs-em-mar24.YRUw2h&refcode=em240318-1-700&t=3&akid=1235%2E135344%2EPPgkha)**

Friend, when I look at this photo of my mom, I think about how much she sacrificed to give my family our American dream.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/81165544/461601251/1820369458?amounts=5,25,50,100&refcode=jtk944-fr-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDYvMS8xMDc1MjUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMWYzZjRmMjAtMjhlNS1lZTExLWFhZjAtMDAyMjQ4MjIzNzk0IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=8naIUi1_4mZSNrzwQjCpl4H1C67C9Zqj2jl_lEyjUeU=)
**When I was 14, my mom made the courageous decision to leave our home in Ecuador and bring my sisters and me to America.** She wanted so badly to give us an incredible education, access to affordable, high-quality health care, and a better life. And she was willing to do anything to make that happen.
When we first arrived in America, my family lived in a small one room apartment. My mom worked hard to pay the bills in those early days, working double shifts as a home health aide, taking English classes at night, and still making time to be an incredible, supportive mom.
I eventually started working at a local doughnut shop in the mornings before school began to help make ends meet. But she never once let our financial difficulties get in the way of my education. She brought us to America to get a chance at a better future, and that started with a strong education.
Because of my mom's sacrifices, her bravery, her support, and her unyielding hope, I was able to graduate high school and college, find a career giving back to my community, and eventually become the first South American immigrant ever elected to Congress. Today, I'm my mom's primary caretaker, and I'm so grateful that I can live with her and give her the care and comfort she deserves after doing so much for my family.
**But there are so many other moms out there who are still struggling to pay the bills, give their kids a shot at a better life, and win their American dream. And every day, that dream is looking further and further out of reach.**

**That's why I'm running for Senate: to give those families the leg up they need. **I'll fight tirelessly to make housing more affordable, increase access to high-quality health care, give more kids the chance to get a college degree, and so much more.

clean_body: she was willing to do anything | | | Friend, when I look at this photo of my mom, I think about how much she sacrificed to give my family our American dream. = When I was 14, my mom made the courageous decision to leave our home in Ecuador and bring my sisters and me to America. She wanted so badly to give us an incredible education, access to affordable, high-quality health care, and a better life. And she was willing to do anything to make that happen. When we first arrived in America, my family lived in a small one room apartment. My mom worked hard to pay the bills in those early days, working double shifts as a home health aide, taking English classes at night, and still making time to be an incredible, supportive mom. I eventually started working at a local doughnut shop in the mornings before school began to help make ends meet. But she never once let our financial difficulties get in the way of my education. She brought us to America to get a chance at a better future, and that started with a strong education. Because of my mom's sacrifices, her bravery, her support, and her unyielding hope, I was able to graduate high school and college, find a career giving back to my community, and eventually become the first South American immigrant ever elected to Congress. Today, I'm my mom's primary caretaker, and I'm so grateful that I can live with her and give her the care and comfort she deserves after doing so much for my family. But there are so many other moms out there who are still struggling to pay the bills, give their kids a shot at a better life, and win their American dream. And every day, that dream is looking further and further out of reach. That's why I'm running for Senate: to give those families the leg up they need. I'll fight tirelessly to make housing more affordable, increase access to high-quality health care, give more kids the chance to get a college degree, and so much more. = Please use the links in this email to start a monthly donation through ActBlue. | | | = | | = | | = | | = Thank you, Debbie | * | | | = Debbie Mucarsel-Powell is a Floridian, South American immigrant, mother, and former Congresswoman.
