Friends, When we say redistricting is a perpetual fight, we’re not kidding. Our goal is to make every election cycle fairer than the last. In the past few months alone, our movement has won new congressional maps in Alabama, Louisiana, and New York, introducing new competitive districts and giving Democrats more chances to flip the five seats needed to win back a majority in the U.S. House of Representatives. [HELP ELECT DEMOCRACY DEFENDERS](https://click.everyaction.com/k/81215035/461737035/2035465204?refcode=EM_20240318_FR_13N_red922_527&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImRmMGRmNjQxLTc0ZTUtZWUxMS1hYWYwLTAwMjI0ODIyMzc5NCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=v0zybVCEL75hxCf3hbAQEwXmQTXno2zfrkbZiWq6hn4=) **This is about more than just control of Congress — it’s about what that majority _means_.** When politicians get to pick their voters, instead of the other way around, deep partisanship is rewarded. Gerrymandered districts allow MAGA extremists to avoid real electoral challenges, even when they... | ❌ Side with violent insurrectionists
❌ Vote for dangerous abortion bans
❌ Attack LGBTQ+ students and families

When more voters are truly represented, we have a better chance to elect Democracy Defenders who will:
✅ Guarantee voting rights
✅ Protect abortion rights (and now, even IVF treatment, apparently!) into law
✅ Defend Americans’ rights to be their true selves and love who they want

When politicians get to pick their voters, instead of the other way around, deep partisanship is rewarded. We don’t have the mainstream media or big tech schilling for us, Peter. subject: The first time we’re doing this since a Republican opponent got in the race against me:

body:
Campaigns are chock-full of surprises, but you can count on some events like clockwork.

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=1965%2E4032634%2EUdG0Fm)
---
Campaigns are chock-full of surprises, but you can count on some events like clockwork. And one of them’s coming up fast. In just a few weeks, we’ll file an official report with the FEC on our fundraising for the last three months. The numbers will be public. **The thing that makes this report so important — and different from all of our previous reports — is that this will be the first time we share our fundraising performance since a Republican opponent entered this race against me.** Our opponent, his GOP supporters, special interests, Big Tech moguls, Wall Street executives, and far-right ideologues will scour our numbers for any signs of weakness. Not just because they want to defeat me for re-election — but also because they want to prove that there isn’t enough momentum for our progressive agenda. And if Republicans win more support and gain more power, they’d have more ability to pass their far-right agenda and block progress on the plans this movement is fighting for. I am fighting with everything I’ve got to defeat their extremism and put power into the hands of working people. But I can’t do it alone. A whole bunch of $3 donations add up fast to demonstrate widespread support for ending Washington corruption, ensuring the right to an abortion, guaranteeing universal child care, getting the wealthy to pay their fair share, tackling corporate price gouging, and making Washington work for working families. [**So, we've got to show our opponents that there’s a big, tough team fighting for this re-election campaign and this mission. And one of the best ways to do that is by making a donation before our March 31 deadline. Can you make a donation of $28 or any amount right now to help make our next FEC fundraising report — the first one we’ll share with an opponent in this race — as strong as possible?**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/1920?amount=28&t=8&akid=1965%2E4032634%2EUdG0Fm)

She has worked hard to make BART more affordable for working families and transit-dependent people like herself.

**➡️ **_**In Texas, Emerge alum, entrepreneur, nonprofit founder, and law school graduate Averie Bishop ran for Texas State House District 112 in the Dallas suburbs.**_ Averie is the daughter of a fifth-generation Texan father and a Filipino immigrant mother. | | Friend, Duty, Honor, Country. The iconic slogan has been woven into the fabric of West Point for[ more than a century](http://links.burchettforcongress.com/u/click?_t=feefb5ad83f24ba4b99ac997c1b47e86&_m=2fb8c785c56c4dfb9e6b7c8870c61bae&_e=wVXaz-mgEzRyL-PyQH0Z08SqTYmej0lT391QDXdBC4aGb7dTK4qrqeYsdpvz1zpFgH0w1dFeTQYCmKY61tKbXCv84WrDpwg_nbnvq0i2qDXpXFuGXOWnOSB8T90sUj8TONrVU1e9a1AcfP_lZQCPidzyOvVVRVQypX_xuEhJ2rOqBIAowF2gr1GhGHmf6mWhYJE51IzanClaz_NoBbvpSw2upuPald8qdO9auwiyhsMxg8_Pwv-tc33_R4QZdtmDBFkv3uAEx3dCVGPWss9MsQiu1wJPjZcNHXhBQs-KxCQ%3D). First adopted in 1898 as part of the academy’s seal, the phrase was also added to the mission statement in [1998](http://links.burchettforcongress.com/u/click?_t=feefb5ad83f24ba4b99ac997c1b47e86&_m=2fb8c785c56c4dfb9e6b7c8870c61bae&_e=wVXaz-mgEzRyL-PyQH0Z07N1o-jMcY754ivMwcXibqu1UMN_Bz8DEK5b9OCVLRkSAJ2-l9L9nWrkNb0MXfwyaUWXCT_SA1KfAc4HAPQOPQw3y74b7Qa5Dvm4yxEUCXMLbY_Z1Jx81JVoxhkIFTLtxzcvhtkm7WcLkQpEMThyc6YGgdfTPZtzzPTHMuzILPHYRJxdmRDeecb9JPWbS8TKMySObT3vjC9R5zqzR79gr18kmRKD-CxQRGGRYQ7EZEV52bU7mU8nr8DtL0WXejMO1rn2G1CC87B5xxf81UwyJgiN2dyYbVZufmBklu3ivpTP). Nearly 10 million people faced unprecedented power outages. Hundreds of people tragically lost their lives to the extreme cold. Thousands more were left without power, heat and access to drinkable water. The devastation rivaled that of the most destructive U.S. hurricanes, highlighting our energy infrastructure's vulnerabilities to extreme weather. One thing was clear: The failure of Texas's power grid was a preventable, man-made disaster. Jane PAC-endorsed Rep. Greg Casar is not waiting for the next crisis. He knows we need to act now. It's why he proposed the Connect the Grid Act — a visionary bill aimed at integrating Texas's power grid with the nation's major electric grids. This initiative seeks to save lives in future natural disasters and increase the use of clean energy, which is crucial for tackling the climate crisis and supporting the growth of renewable energy in Texas and beyond. **This is exactly the kind of forward-thinking action that gets us at the Jane Fonda Climate PAC fired up!** Let's unite and show this climate champion that we have his back in this fight. **[Click here to add your name in support of the Connect the Grid Act and join the movement toward building a stronger, more reliable, and cleaner power grid in Texas.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/81215860/461739884/-2043853935?refcode=ea.0ed3de4b-77e5-ee11-aaf0-002248223794&ms=ea.0ed3de4b-77e5-ee11-aaf0-002248223794&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjBlZDNkZTRiLTc3ZTUtZWUxMS1hYWYwLTAwMjI0ODIyMzc5NCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=0XTzsD9rBWy9FSP9Qgih0nwz7oa_FZSrYLLOECCzMEE=&emci=45f002ee-5be5-ee11-aaf0-002248223794&emdi=0ed3de4b-77e5-ee11-aaf0-002248223794&ceid=4823105)** | [**SIGN THE PETITION**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/81215862/461739886/-2043853935?refcode=ea.0ed3de4b-77e5-ee11-aaf0-002248223794&ms=ea.0ed3de4b-77e5-ee11-aaf0-002248223794&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjBlZDNkZTRiLTc3ZTUtZWUxMS1hYWYwLTAwMjI0ODIyMzc5NCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=0XTzsD9rBWy9FSP9Qgih0nwz7oa_FZSrYLLOECCzMEE=&emci=45f002ee-5be5-ee11-aaf0-002248223794&emdi=0ed3de4b-77e5-ee11-aaf0-002248223794&ceid=4823105)

clean_body: Check this out. | Jane PAC's endorsed climate champions don’t just talk the talk. They take action. 👇 Three years ago, Winter Storm Uri unleashed disaster in Texas. Nearly 10 million people faced unprecedented power outages. Hundreds of people tragically lost their lives to the extreme cold. Thousands more were left without power, heat and access to drinkable water. The devastation rivaled that of the most destructive U.S. hurricanes, highlighting our energy infrastructure's vulnerabilities to extreme weather. One thing was clear: The failure of Texas's power grid was a preventable, man-made disaster. Jane PAC-endorsed Rep. Greg Casar is not waiting for the next crisis. He knows we need to act now. It's why he proposed the Connect the Grid Act — a visionary bill aimed at integrating Texas's power grid with the nation's major electric grids. This initiative seeks to save lives in future natural disasters and increase the use of clean energy, which is crucial for tackling the climate crisis and supporting the growth of renewable energy in Texas and beyond. This is exactly the kind of forward-thinking action that gets us at the Jane Fonda Climate PAC fired up! Let's unite and show this climate champion that we have his back in this fight. | Onward, The Jane Fonda Climate PAC Team | = | = = Follow along: | | ---|---|--- Paid for by Jane Fonda Climate PAC, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee. clean_body: | | | Peter, For months now, WFP champions in Congress have been bracing for a massive wave of outside spending to flood their races — and in Rep. Summer Lee’s district, it’s finally arrived. GOP megadonor Jeffrey Yass’ Moderate PAC has just debuted a $270K ad buy targeting Summer and backing her right-wing challenger. 1 This is the first outside spend in Summer’s district, and it’s no surprise that Yass is behind it. In 2022, he was the fourth-largest Republican donor and a key benefactor to groups that spent millions attacking Summer and other progressives in the midterm elections.2 Now, despite suffering a humiliating defeat after Summer overcame $10 million in attack ads last cycle — he’s back again to try and defeat her. Already, Yass has become the biggest donor in the 2024 election cycle, with $46.4 million spent so far 3, and is also rumored to be Trump’s leading choice for Treasury Secretary if he wins in the presidential election4, single-handedly making him one of the biggest individual threats to our movement this year. Billionaire bosses like Jeffrey Yass are gunning for WFP champions like Summer because they’re scared of the power of our movement. That’s why they try and attack us by spreading the myth that ouragenda for working people is somehow unpopular — when in reality, it’s theirs. Yass’ biggest priorities have been defunding public education, banning abortion, cutting taxes for the wealthiest billionaires in our country, and electing MAGA extremists to do his bidding — all efforts that have been overwhelmingly rejected by voters at the polls, time and again. Meanwhile, Summer is seeking re-election to Congress because she wants to defend our abortion rights and reproductive freedom, continue delivering investments to our public education, and because she wants to pass the OLIGARCH Act to tax extreme wealth, reduce inequality, and invest that money back into our communities. Now, is it any wonder that Yass — who’s avoided more than $1 billion in taxes over the last six years5 and is on the short list of nominees to run Treasury in a second Trump administration — is pouring millions to defeat champions for working people like Summer and prop up extremist MAGA Republicans in 2024? Absolutely not. We can’t let super PACs and the right-wing billionaires who fund them succeed in their plan to decimate the ranks of progressives in Congress and put MAGA Republicans in control of all levers of government. We have to get to work now to win critical Democratic primary elections like Summer Lee’s in PA-12 that start in just a few weeks. Republican billionaires with bottomless pits of money want to unseat WFP champions nationwide, but we know we can stop them if our side has the resources to fight back. name: Jena Griswold
subject: March is Women’s History Month
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Jena for Colorado
body:
https://red.msudenver.edu/2020/colorados-legacy-of-womens-suffrage/ [https://red.msudenver.edu/2020/colorados-legacy-of-womens-suffrage/]
Peter –
Happy Women’s History Month!
In honor of this month, I want to highlight Colorado’s unique women’s suffrage movement. Colorado voters approved women’s right to vote in 1893, 27 years before the 14th Amendment granted the right to some women nationwide and the first time in U.S. history that a popular vote passed women’s suffrage into law.
Not only were women voting in Colorado, but in 1894, women began running for office and serving in Colorado’s General Assembly. This progress was only possible because women like Elizabeth Ensley and Ellis Meredith advocated for these freedoms.
However, even after the 19th Amendment was ratified, it would be decades until Native women and many women of color gained full access to the ballot box.
And the fight for full enfranchisement continues today – as we see a resurgence of voter suppression bills in state legislators across the U.S. Colorado led the nation in women’s suffrage, and we continue to lead the nation on election security, voting rights, and voter turnout.
I’m grateful to stand on the shoulders of the women who fought for the freedoms we get to enjoy today. As the first woman democratic Secretary of State, I hope to continue the legacy of the strong Colorado women who came before me.
Learn more about Colorado’s suffrage movement here. [https://red.msudenver.edu/2020/colorados-legacy-of-womens-suffrage/]
Thank you,
Jena

Home prices are climbing across the country, making purchasing a home even more difficult for first-time buyers. It’s only getting harder for young people — **the average age of first-time buyers spiked to a record-high of 36 in 2022.** That’s why Martin introduced the _First-Time Homebuyer Tax Credit Act_ to ensure working families aren’t shut out of the American dream of owning a house. This bill will set up a refundable tax credit for first-time homebuyers worth up to 10 percent of the purchasing price and give homebuyers the opportunity to get the credit at the time of purchase with support from their mortgage issuer. **[Will you help make housing more affordable by signing on as a co-sponsor to _Martin’s First-Time Homebuyer Tax Credit Act_? clean_body: Will you help make housing more affordable by signing on as a co-sponsor to Martin’s First-Time Homebuyer Tax Credit Act? Home prices are climbing across the country, making purchasing a home even more difficult for first-time buyers. It’s only getting harder for young people — the average age of first-time buyers spiked to a record-high of 36 in 2022. That’s why Martin introduced the First-Time Homebuyer Tax Credit Act to ensure working families aren’t shut out of the American dream of owning a house. This bill will set up a refundable tax credit for first-time homebuyers worth up to 10 percent of the purchasing price and give homebuyers the opportunity to get the credit at the time of purchase with support from their mortgage issuer. | Thank you, Team Heinrich | Paid for by Martin Heinrich for Senate Senator Martin Heinrich is committed to helping New Mexico become a leader in defense, tech, and energy with opportunities in every corner.
